$comment: One reason per vault.prefs command that is NOT surfaced on both clients, i.e.
every row of docs/dev/settings-parity.md whose verdict is not `both`. Each
reason says whether the gap is deliberate or a defect, and which remedy it
needs. A reason whose command has converged fails as stale, and so does a
one-sided command with no entry here: the record is compared BOTH ways.
Every entry also carries its row's MEASURED `desktop|mobile` state in `states`,
and the guard compares that state BOTH ways: a row whose measured state moved
while its verdict stayed one-sided (a `called` binding that became
`bound-no-caller`, say) fails naming the drift, because the verdict alone
cannot tell the three remedies apart and would stay green over a live defect.
A RATCHET: the set may shrink, never grow. `--record` REFUSES to write a grown
set, so the command the failure message suggests cannot be used to make a
regression go away. Locking in a convergence is the only edit it will make.
A fresh `--record` seeds every entry with the placeholder, and the reason check

oneSided.set_active_workspace: Desktop-shaped by nature, expected to stay desktop-only: workspaces are a desktop bottom-bar surface, and no mobile screen reads or writes the active workspace. The binding exists on mobile only so the twin prefs modules keep identical export names (myne-md/myne#486). Recorded rather than deleted for that reason, and recorded here so a future parity audit does not re-open it as a gap.
oneSided.set_auto_tag_enabled: Whole feature absent on mobile: automatic tag suggestion has no mobile surface and no mobile reader, so the phone neither honours nor can set it. The remedy is a feature rather than a row, and it stays desktop-only until that feature is decided. Not a defect this branch introduces or can close.
oneSided.set_bar_items_order: Desktop-shaped by nature: the bottom-bar reorder surface is desktop-only, since resolveBarOrder and reorderByDrop have no mobile caller, so the order is default-only on this client. Twin-parity binding, already recorded as dead in scripts/ipc-binding-callers.json for the same reason.
oneSided.set_cli_enabled: Desktop-shaped by nature, expected to stay desktop-only: the terminal client drives the running desktop over its local command socket, so there is nothing on a phone for this switch to gate. The command stays registered because core/src/plugins/prefs is shared.
oneSided.set_cli_excluded_folders: Desktop-shaped by nature, the set alongside set_cli_enabled: the excluded-folder list bounds what the terminal client may read, and mobile ships no terminal. Its §10.2 class is a monotone egress set, which is why it is deliberately NOT grouped with the AI excluded-folders row that this branch makes authorable on mobile.
oneSided.set_cli_rate_limit_disabled: Desktop-shaped by nature: a rate limit on the local command socket, which mobile does not have. Stays desktop-only with its two cli siblings.
oneSided.set_developer_mode: Desktop-shaped by nature, expected to stay desktop-only: it gates a desktop model-path override, and mobile has no developer group at all. A test asserts that absence deliberately (mobile/tests/developer-mode-absent.test.ts), so the gap is a decision rather than an oversight.
oneSided.set_editor_content_width: Desktop-shaped by nature: a prose-measure preference for the desktop editor's chrome, with no mobile surface and no mobile reader outside the prefs default. Already recorded as dead on mobile in scripts/ipc-binding-callers.json.
oneSided.set_editor_layout: Desktop-shaped by nature: the split-pane layout preference, and the mobile editor has no panes, so nothing reads it. Already recorded as dead on mobile in scripts/ipc-binding-callers.json.
oneSided.set_editor_slash_hidden: No UI on either client: the slash-menu twin of toolbar-customize is an unbuilt follow-up, so the setter has no caller and the pref has no reader anywhere. Recorded rather than deleted because the follow-up owns both halves, and it is one of the two no-ui rows in this projection.
oneSided.set_editor_slash_order: No UI on either client, the order half of the same unbuilt follow-up as set_editor_slash_hidden: no ordering UI and no reader on either client.
oneSided.set_editor_vim_mode: Whole feature absent on mobile: modal editing is a per-device input choice, and mobile has no vim mode, so the phone neither honours nor can set it. The remedy is a feature rather than a row. Not a defect this branch introduces or can close.
oneSided.set_folder_notes_enabled: Whole feature absent on mobile: folder notes have no mobile surface and no mobile reader, so the phone neither honours nor can set the off-switch. The remedy is a feature rather than a row. Not a defect this branch introduces or can close.
oneSided.set_hidden_bar_items: Desktop-shaped by nature: bottom-bar customization, and there is no mobile bar to customize and no mobile reader. Already recorded as dead on mobile in scripts/ipc-binding-callers.json.
oneSided.set_keymap_binding: Desktop-shaped by nature, expected to stay desktop-only: mobile has no keymap surface at all, and nothing on this client reads or writes the pref, not even the prefs default object. Already recorded as dead on mobile in scripts/ipc-binding-callers.json.
oneSided.set_new_note_location: Desktop-shaped by nature: the new-note location preference, and the mobile creation flow offers no location choice and nothing reads the default. Already recorded as dead on mobile in scripts/ipc-binding-callers.json.
oneSided.set_ribbon_items: Desktop-shaped by nature: the rail is how a desktop's chrome is arranged, and mobile has no rail. §10.2 classifies it device-local for exactly that reason, so a synced value would mean nothing on a phone.
oneSided.set_ribbon_visible: Desktop-shaped by nature, the visibility half of set_ribbon_items: mobile has no rail to show or hide. Device-local by §10.2 for the same reason.
oneSided.set_right_panel_active_tab: Desktop-shaped by nature: the right panel is a desktop chrome surface with no mobile equivalent and no mobile reader. Already recorded as dead on mobile in scripts/ipc-binding-callers.json.
oneSided.set_right_panel_hidden_tabs: Desktop-shaped by nature, the same surface as set_right_panel_active_tab: no mobile panel, no mobile reader. Already recorded as dead on mobile in scripts/ipc-binding-callers.json.
oneSided.set_right_panel_tab_order: Desktop-shaped by nature, the third of the right-panel trio: desktop-only panel order, default-only on this client. Already recorded as dead on mobile in scripts/ipc-binding-callers.json.
oneSided.set_show_task_marker: Deliberately absent on mobile rather than a gap, and the choice is recorded here because a hidden control with no reason is indistinguishable from an oversight. The pref is SHARED (ScalarLww, MYND-613) and mobile's note list renders no task marker at all, so the phone inherits the desktop's choice and displays nothing either way; adding the row alone would be the inert control this feature exists to remove. The remedy is the rendering feature (a marker slot on mobile/src/app/flows/editor/chrome/NoteRow.tsx fed by the note's task kind), not a settings row, so the row stays off this client until that lands. See docs/decisions/ui/0694-settings-parity-is-a-shared-roster.md.
oneSided.set_spell_enabled: Deliberately absent on mobile rather than a gap: the client ships no spell backend at all (mobile/src/editor-host.ts omits the host's `spell` slot, so no squiggle can ever be drawn), which is why `spellCheckingAvailable()` in mobile/src/lib/spellSupport.ts returns false and the row is gated rather than live. The row stays visible and states its absence, so the sheet does not confirm a choice nothing applies. Its binding and its write path remain, which is exactly why the absence is recorded rather than measured. See docs/decisions/ui/0694-settings-parity-is-a-shared-roster.md.
oneSided.set_spell_languages: Desktop-shaped by nature: the language set for spell checking, and mobile has no spell backend at all (mobile/src/editor-host.ts resolves the spell service to nothing), so no language picker can exist. The binding is dead on mobile and the row it would have set is gated rather than live; see the settings-parity decision entry.
oneSided.set_startup_open: Desktop-shaped by nature: desktop startup behaviour, and the mobile lifecycle (backgrounding, no cold-start note choice) has no such surface, so nothing reads it. Already recorded as dead on mobile in scripts/ipc-binding-callers.json.
